t: Greyfriars was a Franciscan friary that stood near Newgate from 1225 until 1538, when Henry VIII dissolved it. Its church was one of the largest in London, and it housed a studium, a kind of regional university, which rivalled Oxford as an intellectual centre in the early fourteenth century. William of Ockham was among its community. Many notable people were buried here, including Beatrice, daughter of Henry III, the courtier Sir Kenelm Digby, the naval commander Sir Ralph de Spigurnell, and Richard Hastings, Baron Welles, a favourite of Edward IV.
